concept: llama.cpp bundled revision inside Ollama releases
summary: File `LLAMA_CPP_VERSION` at the Ollama repository root holds a single llama.cpp build tag such as `b11232`.

facts.text: File `LLAMA_CPP_VERSION` at the Ollama repository root holds a single llama.cpp build tag such as `b11232`.

`llama/server/CMakeLists.txt` reads that file, fetches the tagged llama.cpp source with FetchContent, and applies the patches in `llama/compat/` (model shims, clip handlers, hooks). The Dockerfile reads the same file.
A developer can point the build at a local llama.cpp tree with `OLLAMA_LLAMA_CPP_SOURCE`, and skip the patch with `OLLAMA_LLAMA_CPP_SKIP_COMPAT_PATCH`.

Ollama's `llama/README.md` lists what a bump must review: build options, backend discovery symbols, llama-server launch args and log lines Ollama parses, streaming frames, and "speculative/MTP paths".
A user can read the bundled build from any install with `<runner>/llama-server --version`; the Homebrew 0.34.4 runner prints `version: 0.4.1-dev (build 11081, commit 161755f29)`.
2026-05-29: Ollama removes its CGO engines and uses llama-server exclusively for GGML models.

Bumps visible in the file history (all by the same maintainer in the commits read): b9493 (06-03), b9509 (06-04), b9637 (06-15), b9672 (06-17), b9888 (07-06), 08-04, 08-10, 08-12, 08-15, 08-18, b10630 (08-26), b10729 (09-01), b10760 (09-02), b10864 (09-10), b10969 (09-15), an unnumbered "version update" (09-22), b11232 (09-29). That is 17 bumps in about four months, roughly weekly since August.

Patch churn rides along: b10729 regenerated the compat hooks patch because upstream removed a whole-tensor `load_data_for` read; b10969 moved the compat patch into libllama because libllama and libmtmd had duplicate symbols; the 09-22 bump removed the Laguna Metal patch as fixed upstream.

A feature merged into llama.cpp master is not in a given Ollama release until a bump after the merge ships. PR 25592 (hybrid checkpoint restore) is still unmerged upstream, so no Ollama release has it.
The Ollama server's own prompt cache and the MLX engine do not depend on this pin.
The pinned llama-server is built without router support (see the router dossier), so llama.cpp's `--models-max` features are unavailable through Ollama.
Whether the 09-22 "version update" is exactly b11081; the tags v0.34.4 and v0.35.0 both pin b11081, so it very likely is.
Which llama.cpp build the 0.40.0 release will pin; the pre-release tag v0.40.0-rc0 pins b11081.
The Ollama repository root has a file `LLAMA_CPP_VERSION` containing `b11232` on main on 2026-10-04.
`llama/server/CMakeLists.txt` reads the pinned commit from `../../LLAMA_CPP_VERSION` ("shared with Dockerfile") and fetches llama.cpp with FetchContent.
The same CMake file honors the environment variable `OLLAMA_LLAMA_CPP_SOURCE` for a local source tree and the option `OLLAMA_LLAMA_CPP_SKIP_COMPAT_PATCH`.
The root CMake file says GGML inference is provided by llama-server, built separately from "the pinned llama.cpp source".
Release tag v0.33.3 pins b10760.
Release tag v0.34.0 pins b10760.
Release tag v0.34.4 pins b11081.
Release tag v0.35.0 pins b11081.
Release tag v0.35.1 pins b11232.
Pre-release tag v0.40.0-rc0 pins b11081.
The v0.35.1 release notes list "Updated llama.cpp and the MLX engine".
The commit "llama.cpp: version bump b11232" (PR 18652) landed on 2026-09-29.
The 2026-09-22 bump (PR 18577) refined memory-allocation failure log substrings and removed the Laguna Metal patch because upstream fixed it.
The b10729 bump regenerated the compat hooks patch because upstream removed the whole-tensor `load_data_for` read, whose last consumer was llama-quantize.
The b10969 bump moved the compat patch into libllama with exported symbols because upstream build changes created duplicate symbols between libllama and libmtmd.
The 2026-06-04 bump to b9509 brought "upstream Gemma 4 12B multimodal projector fixes for the n_head=0 divide-by-zero crash" on x86, CUDA, Linux and Windows.
The 2026-05-29 commit "runner: Remove CGO engines, use llama-server exclusively for GGML models" is the oldest entry read in the history page.

`llama/README.md` says `LLAMA_CPP_VERSION` pins Ollama's llama.cpp source and that an update can affect model loading, GPU discovery, scheduler inputs, runtime logs, streaming and compatibility patches.
`llama/README.md` tells reviewers of a bump to check "speculative/MTP paths", launch args consumed by `llm/llama_server.go`, and logs for device discovery, offload and memory accounting.
The `llama/` directory on main contains `clef`, `compat` and `server` subdirectories and a README.

Measured on this Mac: the Homebrew Ollama 0.34.4 runner `llama-server --version` prints `version: 0.4.1-dev (build 11081, commit 161755f29)` built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000334 for Darwin arm64, matching the tag's pin.
The Homebrew client warns "client version is 0.35.1" while the server is 0.34.4, so the tag pin for a running server is the server's, not the CLI's.
Inference: lazy-mode (llama.cpp PR 27794, merged 2026-08-27) is in b10729 and later pins, so every Ollama release from v0.34.0 includes it, while v0.33.3 shares the b10760 pin and therefore does too.
Inference: llama.cpp PR 28335 (Gemma 4 vision attention, merged 2026-09-04) is absent from b10760 and present from b11081.
Inference: PR 28751 (merged 2026-09-28) is absent from b11081 and, depending on merge time, may be in b11232.
